Compute associations between TF module scores and clinical metadata

compute.metadata.association.Rd

This function tests for associations between transcription factor (TF) module scores and available clinical traits. Numeric traits are correlated with each module (Pearson or Spearman) and shown as a heatmap. If plot_grid = TRUE, categorical traits (text, factor and TRUE/FALSE columns) are additionally tested with one-way ANOVA (Tukey HSD post-hoc) and shown as boxplot grids. All plots are saved in the Results/ directory, and the tables with the results are returned.

Usage

compute.metadata.association(
  scores,
  coldata,
  pval = 0.05,
  corr_type = "spearman",
  file_name = NULL,
  ncol_grid = NULL,
  plot_grid = FALSE,
  padj = FALSE
)

Arguments

scores

A numeric matrix or data frame of TF module scores across samples. Typically the first element (TFs module matrix) of the output from compute.WTCNA(). Rows represent samples, columns represent TF modules.

coldata

A data frame containing clinical traits (both categorical and numerical) for the same samples. Rows must be the same samples, in the same order, as the rows of scores (checked by name; an error is raised otherwise). Numeric columns are treated as continuous: convert number-coded categories (e.g. a stage coded 1 to 4) to factor to test them as groups.

pval

A numeric threshold (default = 0.05) to determine statistical significance (p-value, or adjusted p-value, <= pval). Only associations with (adjusted) p-values below this threshold are annotated in the heatmap or drawn as boxplots.

corr_type

Correlation used for the numeric traits: "spearman" (default) or "pearson".

file_name

Optional character suffix of the names of the saved plots (NULL by default: no suffix).

ncol_grid

Integer. Number of columns in the grid of association boxplots. If NULL (default), it is set to the ceiling of the square root of the number of panels.

plot_grid

Logical; if TRUE, tests categorical traits with ANOVA and saves boxplot grids. Default is FALSE.

padj

Logical; if TRUE, the p-values are corrected for multiple testing with the Benjamini-Hochberg method, across the modules for each trait, and the adjusted p-values are compared with pval. Default is FALSE.

Value

Invisibly, a list with the results:

  • correlation: matrix of module-trait correlations for the numeric traits (modules x traits).

  • p_value: matrix of their p-values.

  • p_adjusted: matrix of their Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values (equal to p_value with padj = FALSE).

  • anova: data frame with the ANOVA of every module for every categorical trait (trait, module, F, p, p_adjusted); NULL if plot_grid = FALSE.

The elements are NULL when there is no trait of that type. The following files are saved to the Results/ directory:

  • TF.modules_metadata_<file_name>.pdf: a heatmap of module-trait correlations for numeric traits (only associations with p-value <= pval are annotated, with the correlation and its significance: * < 0.05, ** < 0.01, *** < 0.001, **** < 0.0001).

  • ANOVA_boxplot_summary_<file_name>_<trait>.svg (if plot_grid = TRUE): one boxplot grid per categorical trait with the significant modules.

Details

Traits that cannot be tested are skipped with a message: numeric traits without variation, and categorical traits with a single level or with as many levels as samples (e.g. a sample identifier). Categorical traits are only analysed when plot_grid = TRUE; a message lists them otherwise.

The size of the figures is computed from their content (number of modules and traits for the heatmap, number of panels for the boxplot grids), and the y-axis of each boxplot panel from its data.

Examples


data("network.tuto")
data("traitdata.tuto")

# The clinical traits of the tutorial data are categorical: they are tested with plot_grid = TRUE
res <- compute.metadata.association(
  scores = network.tuto[[1]],
  coldata = traitdata.tuto,
  pval = 0.05,
  file_name = 'Tutorial',
  plot_grid = TRUE
)
#> Error in ggplot2::ggsave(paste0("Results/ANOVA_boxplot_summary", if (!is.null(file_name)) paste0("_",     file_name), "_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._ -]", "_", tr), ".svg"),     plot = p, device = grDevices::svg, width = max(5, 3.2 * min(ncol_trait,         n_panels) + 0.5), height = 3.4 * ceiling(n_panels/ncol_trait) +         1.4, limitsize = FALSE): Cannot find directory Results.
#> ℹ Please supply an existing directory or use `create.dir = TRUE`.
